facts.claim: Backend source under src/main/java/com/pubginsight/ contains feature packages player/, match/, insight/, history/, health/, common/ (config+exception) and client/ with subpackages pubg/, gemini/, s3/, dynamodb/.

PlayerController exposes GET /api/players/{name} and GET /api/players/{playerId}/season-stats; MatchController exposes GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId}; InsightController exposes GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId}/insights; HistoryController exposes POST and GET .../matches/{matchId}/history; HealthController exposes GET /health.

Frontend services call exactly: GET /health (App.tsx), GET /api/players/{name} and GET /api/players/{playerId}/season-stats (playerService/seasonStatsService), GET /api/players/{playerId}/matches/{matchId} (matchService), GET .../insights (insightService). No frontend service currently calls the /history endpoint - HistoryController exists in the backend but is not yet wired to any UI.
The frontend has exactly one external call surface: src/api/axios.ts, a shared axios instance with baseURL = VITE_API_BASE_URL. It never calls PUBG/Gemini/AWS directly.

Compile-time dependencies: player -> client.pubg; match -> client.pubg; match -> client.s3; insight -> player, insight -> match, insight -> client.gemini; history -> match, history -> insight, history -> client.dynamodb. common.exception depends on (catches exceptions from) player, match, client.pubg, client.gemini, client.dynamodb - the reverse of a typical dependency direction, a deliberate design choice (D1) so feature packages stay independent of each other.

PUBG Developer API and Google Gemini API are both live external integrations: PubgApiClient (rate-limited via PubgRateLimiter, sliding 60s window, blocking) and GeminiApiClient are implemented, called over real HTTPS with Bearer token / API key respectively, and verified working end-to-end against real data (Feature 1 Player Search and Feature 2 Match Analytics verified live per PROJECT_CONTEXT.md; Feature 3 AI Insights code complete).

CORRECTED 2026-09-13: client.s3 (S3MatchCacheClient, cache-aside for match JSON, soft-fail on error per D12) and client.dynamodb (AnalysisHistoryRepository, analysis-history persistence, hard-fail/502 on error per D12) are now DEPLOYED AND VERIFIED against the real personal AWS account. PROJECT_CONTEXT.md's Current Status section states: 'DynamoDB table (pubg-insight-analysis-history) and S3 bucket (pubg-insight-match-cache) created on the personal AWS account and verified working end-to-end against real AWS' - confirmed via a real GET .../matches/{id} called twice showing a visible speedup on the second call with no S3Exception warnings (cache-aside working), and a real POST .../matches/{id}/history followed by GET .../history round-tripping a real item through DynamoDB. TASK.md line 65 was updated to match: 'Create the DynamoDB table and S3 bucket - done and verified'. This supersedes an earlier reading of these same docs (pre-correction) that had said bucket/table creation was still pending - that was based on a stale doc snapshot.

Elastic Beanstalk, API Gateway, Lambda, and Athena have no application code and no created infrastructure at all yet - purely planned/approved in the architecture (approved AWS service list in PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, worth the maximum 25 rubric points for criterion 3 if all six services are automated), not built.

PUBG rate limiting is enforced backend-side by PubgRateLimiter (D16): a single shared component tracks a sliding 60s window of call timestamps and blocks the calling thread until a slot is free, protecting the app's one shared PUBG API key budget (10 req/min) regardless of which frontend tab/request triggered the call.

Real, official-source icons were resolved and synced into this project's asset manifest for: Amazon S3, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon Athena (extracted directly from the official AWS Architecture Service Icons ZIP, bypassing a bug in nexcanvas's own --provider aws-official --source-archive filename-discovery step that could pick a __MACOSX/._ AppleDouble junk duplicate over the real SVG when both share a near-identical normalized filename); React (from Simple Icons); Spring Boot and Google Gemini and PUBG (from Simple Icons, fetched live from the jsdelivr CDN and each verified via its embedded <title> tag before syncing). All are recorded as 'Synced' (React additionally reached 'Embedded' in a prior build) in assets/asset_manifest.json.

assumptions: The app's own custom code (feature packages health/player/match/insight/history, and the client.pubg/client.gemini/client.s3/client.dynamodb wrapper classes) is not a named product with a logo, so these remain generic labeled glyphs even though the systems they call now have real icons.

The diagram models frontend as a single Container-level node (React Frontend) rather than breaking out individual components (PlayerSearch.tsx, MatchList.tsx, etc.) - the requested viewIntent is system/component architecture for the backend; frontend internal component structure is out of scope for this diagram.
exclusions: Frontend's newer V2-redesign components observed in the sibling repo (PerformanceRadar.tsx, PlayerIdentityCard.tsx, DeltaIndicator.tsx, PerformanceBreakdown.tsx, AiInsights.tsx, RevealOnMount.tsx, StatTile.tsx, SectionTitle.tsx) are not individually modeled - they are all still served through the same single axios call surface and same backend controllers documented above, so they don't change the architecture-level picture this diagram shows.

Sequence-level detail (request/response steps within a single feature call) is intentionally excluded - already fully documented as Mermaid sequence diagrams in docs/deliverables/ARCHITECTURE.md; this diagram's viewIntent is architecture (system context + component view), not sequence.
